Household Water Insecurity and Drinking Water Service Levels from the KALAI Project in Nampula, Mozambique
text: dataset kalaiwash contains one row per household interview. 275 observations 40 variables. overview variable names, see following table. options column lists levels categorical variable. Variables calculated original Excel workbook (jmp_improved, jmp_water_service, total_collect_time, total_liters, liters_person, hwise_score hwise_insecurity_level) recalculated R raw survey responses verified Excel values. 12 HWISE items ordered factors whose levels refer number times last four weeks: Never (0), Rarely (1–2), Sometimes (3–10), Often (11–20) Always (20). HWISE score sums 12 items scored Never 0, Rarely 1, Sometimes 2, Often Always 3. insecurity levels follow Frongillo et al. (2024): --marginal (0–2), Low (3–11), Moderate (12–23) High (24–36).

code: library(kalaiwash) library(dplyr)  kalaiwash |>    count(survey_type, jmp_water_service) |>    group_by(survey_type) |>    mutate(share = round(100 * n / sum(n))) |>    ungroup() |>    knitr::kable(col.names = c("Survey", "JMP service level", "Households", "Share (%)")) kalaiwash |>    count(survey_type, hwise_insecurity_level) |>    group_by(survey_type) |>    mutate(share = round(100 * n / sum(n))) |>    ungroup() |>    knitr::kable(col.names = c("Survey", "HWISE insecurity level", "Households", "Share (%)"))

title: kalaiwash: Household water insecurity and drinking water service levels from the KALAI project in Nampula, Mozambique — kalaiwash
text: Baseline (November 2024) endline (June 2025) household survey data KALAI water, sanitation hygiene project HELVETAS Larde, Memba, Moma Mecuburi districts, Nampula Province, Mozambique. row one household interview. Variables cover primary drinking water source /UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme (JMP) service level, water collection times volumes, sanitation handwashing practices, 12 items Household Water Insecurity Experiences (HWISE) Scale summary score (0 36) insecurity level. HWISE items ordered factors whose levels refer number times last four weeks: Never (0), Rarely (1 2), Sometimes (3 10), Often (11 20) Always (20). Derived variables recalculated R raw survey responses checked original Excel calculations; see data-raw/data_processing.R.
